description: This topic explains the difference between weather and climate, the elements of weather and the instruments used to measure them, the layout of a weather station, how weather data is recorded and interpreted, and the factors that influence the climate of a place.

mcq.questionText: Which statement best describes the difference between weather and climate?

options.text: Weather is the average condition of the atmosphere over many years, while climate is the day-to-day condition
Weather is the condition of the atmosphere at a particular place and time, while climate is the average weather over a long period
Weather and climate mean exactly the same thing
Weather only refers to rainfall, while climate only refers to temperature

mcq.explanation: Weather is the short-term, day-to-day state of the atmosphere, whereas climate is the average weather condition of a place observed over a long period, usually 30 years or more.

mcq.questionText: Which instrument is used to measure atmospheric pressure?
mcq.explanation: A barometer measures atmospheric pressure, while the thermometer measures temperature, the hygrometer measures humidity and the rain gauge measures rainfall.

mcq.questionText: Which element of weather is measured using a rain gauge?
mcq.explanation: A rain gauge collects and measures the amount of rainfall received at a place, usually recorded in millimetres.

mcq.questionText: The instrument used to measure the direction of the wind is the:
mcq.explanation: A wind vane shows the direction from which the wind is blowing, while the anemometer measures wind speed.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following is NOT an element of weather?
mcq.explanation: Soil type is a characteristic of the land surface, not an atmospheric condition. Temperature, humidity and cloud cover are all elements of weather.

mcq.questionText: Why is a weather station usually located in an open area away from buildings and tall trees?

options.text: To make it easy to take photographs
To allow the instruments to record true conditions of the free atmosphere without obstruction
Because instruments cannot work near buildings
To keep the instruments hidden from people

mcq.explanation: Buildings and trees can block wind, give shade and affect temperature and rainfall readings, so an open site ensures the instruments record the true state of the atmosphere.

mcq.questionText: The Stevenson screen is used in a weather station mainly to:

options.text: Hold and protect thermometers and the hygrometer from direct sunlight and rain
Measure the speed of the wind
Record the number of sunshine hours

mcq.explanation: The Stevenson screen is a white louvred box that shelters temperature and humidity instruments from direct sunlight and rain while allowing free air circulation.

mcq.questionText: Why is a Stevenson screen painted white and built with louvred (slatted) sides?

options.text: White paint absorbs heat and the slats keep out air
White reflects sunlight to avoid heating, and the louvres allow free movement of air around the instruments
To make it attractive and easy to clean
To trap heat so the thermometer reads higher

mcq.explanation: The white colour reflects sunlight to prevent the box from heating up, and the louvred sides let air flow freely so the thermometers measure the true air temperature.

mcq.questionText: Which pair of instruments together can be used to find the relative humidity of the air?
mcq.explanation: A hygrometer uses a wet-bulb and a dry-bulb thermometer; the difference in their readings is used to determine the relative humidity of the air.

mcq.questionText: The maximum and minimum temperatures of a day are recorded using a:
mcq.explanation: A Six's thermometer, also called the maximum-minimum thermometer, records both the highest and lowest temperatures reached during a period.

mcq.questionText: Which factor explains why areas near the Equator are generally hot throughout the year?

options.text: They are far from the sea
The sun's rays strike the Equator almost vertically, giving intense heating
They are at very high altitude
They receive only cold ocean currents

mcq.explanation: Near the Equator the sun is almost overhead, so its rays strike the ground vertically and concentrate heat over a small area, producing high temperatures all year.

mcq.questionText: As one climbs up a high mountain, the temperature usually:
mcq.explanation: Temperature falls with altitude because the air becomes thinner and holds less heat, which is why mountain tops such as Kilimanjaro are cold and snow-capped.

mcq.questionText: How do warm ocean currents influence the climate of nearby coastal areas?

options.text: They make the coast colder and drier
They warm the air above them, raising temperatures and often bringing rainfall to the coast
They have no effect on climate at all
They only change the colour of the sea

mcq.explanation: Warm currents heat the air above the sea, raising coastal temperatures and increasing evaporation, which can bring more rainfall to the nearby land.

mcq.questionText: Cloud cover in a weather station is usually measured or estimated in units called:
mcq.explanation: Cloud cover is estimated in oktas, where the sky is divided into eight parts and the observer notes how many eighths are covered by cloud.

mcq.questionText: On a weather record, the average temperature of a day is best found by:

options.text: Adding the maximum and minimum temperatures and dividing by two
Subtracting the minimum from the maximum temperature
Multiplying the maximum by the minimum temperature

mcq.explanation: The mean daily temperature is calculated by adding the day's maximum and minimum temperatures and dividing the sum by two.

fib.questionText: The condition of the atmosphere of a place at a particular time is called _____.
fib.explanation: Weather refers to the short-term, day-to-day state of the atmosphere of a place.

fib.questionText: The average weather condition of a place recorded over a long period of time is called _____.
fib.explanation: Climate is the average of weather conditions taken over a long period, usually about 30 years or more.

fib.questionText: The instrument used to measure air temperature is the _____.
fib.explanation: A thermometer measures temperature, commonly in degrees Celsius.

fib.questionText: The amount of water vapour present in the atmosphere is known as _____.
fib.explanation: Humidity is the measure of water vapour in the air and is recorded using a hygrometer.

fib.questionText: The speed of the wind is measured using an instrument called an _____.
fib.explanation: An anemometer measures wind speed, often shown by spinning cups that turn faster in stronger wind.

fib.questionText: The white louvred box that houses thermometers in a weather station is called a _____.
fib.explanation: The Stevenson screen protects temperature and humidity instruments from direct sunlight and rain while allowing free air flow.

fib.questionText: The number of hours of bright sunshine received in a day is recorded using a _____ recorder.
fib.explanation: A sunshine recorder (such as the Campbell-Stokes type) burns a trace on a card to show the hours of bright sunshine.

fib.questionText: The height of a place above sea level, which affects its temperature, is called _____.
fib.explanation: Altitude influences climate because temperature decreases as height above sea level increases.

fib.questionText: The distance of a place north or south of the Equator, which strongly affects its climate, is called its _____.
fib.explanation: Latitude affects the angle at which the sun's rays strike the surface, so places near the Equator are hotter than those near the poles.

fib.questionText: Rainfall amounts collected by a rain gauge are usually measured in _____.
fib.explanation: The depth of rainfall caught in a rain gauge is measured in millimetres (mm).

tf.questionText: Weather can change from hour to hour, but climate stays the same for a very long time.
tf.explanation: Weather is short-term and changeable, while climate describes the long-term average and changes only very slowly.

tf.questionText: A barometer is used to measure the amount of rainfall received at a place.
tf.explanation: A barometer measures atmospheric pressure; rainfall is measured using a rain gauge.

tf.questionText: Temperature generally decreases as altitude increases.
tf.explanation: As one goes higher above sea level the air becomes thinner and colder, so temperature falls with altitude.

tf.questionText: A wind vane is used to measure the speed of the wind.
tf.explanation: A wind vane shows wind direction; wind speed is measured by an anemometer.

tf.questionText: Areas near the Equator generally experience higher temperatures than areas near the poles.
tf.explanation: Near the Equator the sun's rays strike almost vertically, giving more concentrated heating than at the poles where rays are slanting.

tf.questionText: The Stevenson screen should be painted black so that it absorbs heat for accurate readings.
tf.explanation: The Stevenson screen is painted white so it reflects sunlight and does not heat up, allowing thermometers to record the true air temperature.

tf.questionText: Relative humidity can be found by comparing the readings of a wet-bulb and a dry-bulb thermometer.
tf.explanation: The difference between the wet-bulb and dry-bulb thermometer readings is used to determine the relative humidity of the air.

tf.questionText: Cloud cover is measured by collecting clouds in a container and weighing them.
tf.explanation: Cloud cover cannot be collected; it is estimated by observation in oktas, the eighths of the sky that are covered by cloud.

tf.questionText: Distance from the sea is one of the factors that influence the climate of a place.
tf.explanation: Places near the sea have a moderate climate, while inland places tend to have hotter summers and colder winters due to continentality.

tf.questionText: The mean daily temperature is found by adding the maximum and minimum temperatures and dividing by two.
tf.explanation: Adding the day's highest and lowest temperatures and dividing by two gives the average (mean) temperature for that day.

summary.correctAnswer: The atmospheric condition of a place at a particular time
summary.explanation: Weather is short-term and can change quickly from hour to hour or day to day.

summary.correctAnswer: The average weather of a place over a long period (about 30 years)
summary.explanation: Climate describes the usual long-term atmospheric conditions of a place.

summary.correctAnswer: Temperature, rainfall, humidity, pressure, wind, sunshine and cloud cover
summary.explanation: These atmospheric conditions are observed and measured at a weather station.
The barometer measures the weight of the air pressing on the Earth's surface.
It collects rainwater and the amount is read off in millimetres.

summary.correctAnswer: To shelter thermometers and the hygrometer from direct sunlight and rain
summary.explanation: Its white colour and louvred sides allow free air flow and prevent overheating for accurate readings.

summary.correctAnswer: Anemometer for speed and wind vane for direction
summary.explanation: Together they describe how strong the wind is and where it is coming from.

summary.correctAnswer: Places near the Equator are hotter than places near the poles
summary.explanation: The angle of the sun's rays is more vertical near the Equator, giving stronger heating.

summary.correctAnswer: Temperature decreases as height above sea level increases
summary.explanation: Higher places like mountain tops are colder than lowlands.

summary.correctAnswer: Latitude, altitude, distance from the sea, ocean currents, winds and relief
summary.explanation: These factors together determine the temperature and rainfall pattern of a place.

hoq.questionText: A town located on the coast and another town far inland are at the same latitude. Which statement best explains the likely difference in their climates?

options.text: Both towns will have exactly the same temperature range because they share a latitude
The coastal town will have a smaller temperature range and more moisture, while the inland town will have hotter days, colder nights and a larger range
The inland town will always be cooler and wetter than the coastal town
The coastal town will be much drier than the inland town

hoq.explanation: The sea heats and cools slowly, so it moderates coastal temperatures and adds moisture, while inland areas experience greater extremes due to continentality.

hoq.questionText: A weather observer records a maximum temperature of 30 degrees Celsius and a minimum of 18 degrees Celsius for a day. What are the daily temperature range and the mean daily temperature?

options.text: Range 12 degrees and mean 24 degrees Celsius
Range 48 degrees and mean 12 degrees Celsius
Range 24 degrees and mean 12 degrees Celsius
Range 12 degrees and mean 48 degrees Celsius

hoq.explanation: The range is the maximum minus the minimum (30 - 18 = 12), and the mean is the sum divided by two ((30 + 18) / 2 = 24).

hoq.questionText: Two stations at the same latitude record very different temperatures: Station X is cool while Station Y is hot. Station X is on a high plateau. What most likely explains this difference?

options.text: Station X receives more sunshine hours
Station X is at a higher altitude, so its temperature is lower than the lowland Station Y
Station Y is closer to the poles
Station X has fewer clouds than Station Y

hoq.explanation: Since both stations share the same latitude, the difference is best explained by altitude, because temperature decreases as height above sea level increases.
